    Six Plays, Endless Laughs

    Ezra Torres, Student Reporter • November 10, 2026
    https://www.sanjac.edu/programs/areas-of-study/arts/theatre-film/south/
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 3:46
    Instaread

    What do Shakespeare, an ice-climbing axe and a made-up language have in common? They all appear in San Jacinto College’s upcoming production of All in the Timing. San Jac’s South Campus Department of Theatre and Film is currently presenting All in the Timing from Nov. 5-14 at the Black Box Theatre in the Flickinger Fine Arts Center. The production is part of the department’s Fall season productions. Tickets are $3 for San Jac students, $5 for San Jac faculty and staff,  and $7 for community members.

    “All in the Timing is a collection of six short plays by David Ives that present a whole range of comedic absurdity,” says Tanar Yocum, the plays Director.

    The production explores relationships, language and time through humor and unexpected situations. The theater department wanted a play by a modern American playwright that would
    challenge students without overwhelming them. It also needed to be engaging and easy to divide among multiple directors. All in the Timing met those goals while giving the department a chance
    to try a different approach. 

    “Recent productions have leaned into concepts and ideas that have led to large, immersive sets that really make you feel like you’re looking into an abandoned mall, a honky-tonk diner, or even the Brio Superfund site,” says Yocum, “this time around, we’re focusing on the human elements of the show and performing in the round to allow audiences to experience the show and connect with its messages from anywhere in the room.”

    Instead of relying on large sets, the production will focus on the actors and their performances. The theater-in-the-round setup will also give audience members different views of the stage.
    As opening night approaches, the cast, directors and crew are working together to prepare the production. The actors continue to develop their scenes while the crew works behind the
    scenes.

    “Our crew members do amazing work in the background to support our designers based on the discoveries the actors and directors have been making in rehearsals,” says Yocum.

    According to Yocum, one of the most rewarding parts of directing has been discovering new ideas with the cast and designers. 

    “There is a magic to the discovery process, and working with actors and designers to make those discoveries together can lead to a much stronger show than you could have ever imagined on your own,” says Yocum.

    Yocum believes the production has something for everyone. The six plays use different levels of absurdity to create unexpected moments and plenty of opportunities to laugh.

    “It’s hard to narrow down specifics because it has such varying levels of absurdity that I think everyone will find something they can laugh about and will leave an impression on them,” says Yocum.

    Beyond the humor, Yocum hopes audiences will leave with new thoughts about time and how they spend it.

    “I hope that anyone who sees this production walks away feeling entertained, obviously, but more importantly I hope they walk away with some new thoughts on the time we have on this earth, how we spend it, and what time really means when it moves beyond our perspectives,” says Yocum.

    All in the Timing offers a chance to experience live performance. Unlike movies, theater happens in front of the audience, making each performance different.

    “What makes theatre different and worth your time is that it’s live and it’s right in front of you,” says Yocum, “the actors are real people who can make mistakes and they never do it exactly the same way twice, and it feels like anything is possible in those moments,” says Yocum.

    Marie Spencer Flickinger Fine Arts Center (S15.151) is located at San Jacinto College South Campus 13735 Beamer Road, Houston, TX 77089

    For more information visit https://www.sanjac.edu/programs/areas-of-study/arts/theatre-film/south/
